Another test I wanted to do was using hit markers. A common piece of feedback I often got was that, in multiplayer, it wasn't always apparent who got the killing blow on an enemy.

Now any damaging hit that you make on an enemy will display a blue hit marker.
http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/25423482/a234c7b7842c5e169c06895defd46a11c56a908f.png

The goal of this is to display feedback to the user without ruining the immersion of the game and the fantasy setting, so please let me know if you like/dislike the system, and how it might be improved!

Anti-Harassment Measures

Two issues were brought to my attention as methods for harassing players. Both of which should now be resolved with no action needing to be taken against offenders.

My philosophy is (and will continue to be) that it is much better to remove the ability to harass than to punish those who partake in it.

 Hands in Face


Other players' hands that come close to your head will now fade away (with a lower distance threshold) in the same way your own hands fade when moving them close to your own head.

 Arrows in Helmet


Shooting arrows into other players helmets is meant to be a fun and good-humored interaction. Continually I see new players to the game are delighted when they shoot an arrow into their team mates head, and the other player reaches up and attempts to pull it out.

However, with that interaction, harassment is possible, so a new option has been added to the gameplay settings called "Personal Bubble". Turning this on immediately destroys any arrow that comes in contact with you but only on your screen. 

The other players still see an arrow stick into your head/bow/quiver, but it will no longer be visible to you as the targeted player, this allows everyone to have their fun while keeping frustration to a minimum.

Note: As always, multiplayer functions are difficult to test, so please let me know if any weird edge cases arise that don't work as intended!

notes.title: Alpha 0.10.3
notes.content:
Now that I'm back from a relaxing holiday weekend with family, I think I'll be able to get back to a more consistent update schedule.

This update has a number of fixes as well as a highly requested multiplayer feature.

Friends List Integration
http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/25423482/ec8a288ae2e3fc36891495f582dfd14a118c0200.png

From the multiplayer menu, the disabled "Create Private Game" has been replaced with "Play With Friends". Pressing it will open up the friends list populated with your Steam Friends. While a fair bit of work has been done to make sure nothing acts differently, there may be some edge cases I didn't find, so let me know if there is unusual connecting/disconnecting behavior!

    FPS counter added to graphics settings menu

Working on a new Gameplay Lab that is significantly more extensive. Not sure when it will be added but a lot of time is being spent on it as this is the first time that there is the potential to make people motion sick, so we want all the options to go through some vetting before subjecting players to them :)

notes.title: Alpha 0.10.2
notes.content:
This update has a number of changes to the Voice Chat system.

Voice Chat Options
http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/25423482/2851ca5ecc2ab530da915fcd4f5326e7cfecd09c.png

With a number of people asking for voice chat options, I spent today working on a system that gives as much information as possible while not cluttering the space.

As you can see from the image above, a Speaker is now beside each player's name on the scoreboard.

Under normal circumstances, each player's icon will be white with the exception of your own, which will be blue. The speaker will be enabled or disabled depending on that player's voice-chat setting (including your own).

If for some reason a player doesn't realize there mic is on and is having a conversation you'd rather not hear, or any other reason, you can now mute that player by shooting an arrow at their speaker icon on the scoreboard.

A player that you have explicitly muted will use the disabled icon, and also turn red to indicate that the mute is for a reason. This action is not saved between sessions yet as it is just an experiment at the moment. 

Also you can not shoot your own speaker to turn your mic on/off, so the settings menu is still the place to go, but it makes it much easier to see your current Voice Chat status.

I was able to test this a bit in a multiplayer game and everything seems to be working as intended. But as always please let me know if an issue arises that I didn't catch!

 Other Changes 

The speaking particles should also now be visible to display on players that are currently speaking.

And as a result of the scoreboard change, players with long names should no longer have their names clipped into the side of the keep, and instead will be scaled down in size to fit their container.

notes.title: Alpha 0.10.1
notes.content:
Just got back from San Francisco this afternoon, and I think I've had enough of a breather to push out a new update tonight ;)

This one has some usability improvements and bug fixes.

Updates and Fixes

    Fixed gems showing up when they shouldn't in multiplayer
    Fixed error regarding EnemyBase.cs:346
    Fixed most cases of stingray physics anomalies
    Temporarily removed enemy "Deathrattle" until a more visually appealing system is implemented
    Fixed error regarding Quiver.cs:196
    Increased size of enemies in Gamelpay Lab for easier testing
    Increased hitbox for lighting arrows on fire
    Arrow feathers have received a temporary texture


Bow and Quiver Interaction

During my trip, we tested the game with a number of people who had little VR experience. One of the conclusions reached was that the action of dropping/swapping the bow, and moving the quiver by hand, was really unintuitive.

For this reason the bow and quiver are no longer droppable/swappable/movable using the controllers, and instead are determined by the settings menu (changing the settings will now immediately change the desired effect, either right/left hand holding bow, or shoulder/hip mounted quiver)

Being able to throw the bow around was something that a number of people enjoyed, so I will be working on adding other easily accessible interactive objects to the game to play with during downtime.

Note: There is still an issue present where hitting the system menu button will drop the bow onto the ground. For usability reasons, the method to pick it up has been changed to the trigger, which is more intuitive for new users but also might confuse the more seasoned players.

notes.title: Alpha 0.9.3
notes.content:
Another more serious bug fix

Fixes

    Fixed teleporter not responding to arrows


Turned out that it was treating the arrows as being "deflected", so I've introduced a new counter to see how many times an arrow has been deflected instead of just an yes/no.

This also means that I was able to add it to the score, so a shot that bounces twice before hitting an enemy is now worth more than a shot that only bounces once :)

notes.title: Alpha 0.8.11
notes.content:
Couple changes before starting work on this weekend's larger update.

Versioning

Right off the bat you may notice that this update looks different than in the past, that's because I'm not using letters anymore! Before I went too far down the rabit hole I've made the switch to something more along the lines of the Semantic Versioning. 

It's a bit different since I don't have a public API, so the basic idea is that Patch versions (Z in X.Y.Z) are for bug fixes and minor changes. Minor versions (Y in X.Y.Z) are for medium additions to the core game mechanics and systems (Expect one of these once a week). And Major versions (X in X.Y.Z) are for large additions in content or major changes in game system.

The X will only change after alpha and beta have ended, so until that point Minor version increases will handle both medium and large changes.

VRTK 2.1

This update moves to VRTK 2.1 (and also puts the github repository for VRTK right inside the project itself, so it's easy to grab the latest changes and it won't require these big announcements anymore, we'll just always be up to date).

A fair bit was changed, so please let me know if any of the interactions are incorrect like when we upgraded to 2.0!

Other Changes

    Arrow catching fire sound was removed
    Enemies will correctly attack the door even if no one is watching


Edit:
Also fixed issue introduced that stopped bow/quiver from being picked up after dropping.

notes.title: Alpha 0.8.9
notes.content:
New effects and settings for today's update

Super Sampling Slider

The video settings panel gets its first option today with a super sampling slider (thanks to Pool Nation for the great idea!). The range goes from 0.8 to 2.0 with a default of 1. Updates are realtime once you release the slider, no need to reload the game and it should be immediately evident. 

Please keep in mind that super sampling is incredibly resource intensive. Even the new Titan X probably can't do much more than 2.0 without Reprojection kicking in, so don't feel bad if you can't boost it up too much with a  new graphics card.

Fog

The current scene felt a bit too "happy" with the ghouls and monster's that are coming at you, so this update tests out a new fog effect.

There are two effects in the game, one on the loading scene, and one in the game. I'd like feedback about which one you guys like the best.

Loading Scene: Screen Space Fog - This is a fullscreen camera effect that takes the entire image and passes it through a 'fog filter' using the distance information to decide how much 'fog' (sky color) to apply.

Game Scene: Particle Fog - This effect uses a particle system (really large faint blue/gray circles) to cover a certain area with fog. At the moment it's above the canyon and where enemies spawn.

Both of these effects have different advantages and disadvantages, the screenspace fog can't be easily animated, but the particle fog requires 'soft particles' which are expensive (not that the screen space is cheap). So getting player feedback about which fog feels the best would be helpful!

Additional Changes and Fixes

     Fixed error on startup with AzureSky.cs
     Re-enabled the snow effect

notes.title: Alpha 0.8.8
notes.content:
Some larger changes today to replace the loading scene, and another try at getting purchasable talents to work well.

New Loading Scene
http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/25423482/832c542900cd0b1b02a90921e577f1494c93a478.png

After clearing out the project of extraneous assets (from over 20GB down to 10), I forgot about the loading scene and removed all the rocks that were used. Figured that this was the perfect time to make a more thematically appropriate loading scene.

Still has a few grabbable rocks to play around while you wait!

Talent Currency

One of the biggest issues with using the score as currency for talents is being competitive. You don't want to lose the hard earned points by spending them on something, especially if you're at the top of the leaderboard.

For that reason, I've introduced a new currency system that's directly tied to score. Every point you get gives you 1 'currency', when you purchase a talent though, the currency is deducted, not your score. You can see your current currency inside the big orb at the bottom of the talent tree.

Other Changes

     Decreased volume of ignite effect
     Disabled tutorial button (tutorial is broken because of talents)

notes.title: Alpha 0.8.6
notes.content:
Number of changes for this weekend's larger update

Talent Purchasing

This update tests out the mechanic of purchasing talents with the score you have accrued throughout the siege. They are non-permanent, so you will be purchasing talents each time you play.

All talents are now immediately available, but have an associated 'Cost' in points. Purchasable talents (for which you have enough points) will be displayed with a different color.

You are not restricted to purchasing a talent in Tier 1 to unlock Tier 2, however talents in Tier 2 are more expensive.

If you purchase a talent in a tier, you may switch to another talent in the same tier by purchasing it as well. This will deactivate the previously chosen talent, but switching back will be free.

Other Additions/Changes

    Audio cues for Starting/Stopping a game
    Audio cue for next wave
    Animated effect on spectator and talent system
    Multiplayer teammates visible through walls

notes.title: Alpha 0.8.3
notes.content:
Trying out a new bow interaction system that a number of people have requested.

Bow/Quiver Setup

Previously every time you opened op the game or entered/left a multiplayer, you would have to grab the bow and quiver off the ground. This is no longer the case.

When starting the game up for the first time now, you will be presented with your Bow and Quiver floating out of reach, with a message asking you to select your dominant hand with a trigger press.

Doing so will immediately set you up with the bow and quiver equipped (bow going in your non-dominant hand, quiver attached to your shoulder), as well as saving your preference for dominant hand (which can be changed in Settings -> Gameplay -> Hands).

Once the setting has been saved, every time you open up the app or enter/leave a multiplayer game your bow and quiver will equip themselves.

Note: I know that some people like the quiver on their hip, but I think it's a minority and actually many people didn't know it could even be placed on the shoulder. An option will eventually be added to determine which spot (hip/shoulder) you would like the quiver to auto-equip to. But at least currently it's slightly easier to move from shoulder -> hip than pick it up from the ground.

Other Fixes


    The Audio settings correctly work again


Let me know if I overlooked anything, and if a serious bug occurs (like yesterday's Bow being broken) don't hesitate to email me at support@alvios.com

notes.title: Alpha 0.8.1
notes.content:
Two highly requested features now make their way into the settings menu.

Hand Calibration

Using the Settings -> Gameplay -> Hands menu, you can now calibrate your right and left gloves individually to ensure that they are correctly lined up with their real world counterparts.

Your settings are saved immediately, but you can always revert back to the default placement.

Draw Offset Toggle

Un-checking this option (also in Settings -> Gameplay -> Hands) will stop your arrow drawing hand from offsetting away from the controller as you pull it closer to your face. 

While the intent of the offset is to prevent hitting your headset when drawing an arrow to eye level, numerous people have requested the option to turn the offset off for a more 1-to-1 experience, especially if they have practiced archery.

These are fairly untested features, so if there are any unintended side effects from adjusting the hands in edge case scenarios, please let me know.

notes.title: Alpha 0.8.0
notes.content:
This weeks big update has two new additions (not including the new enemy system already released on Friday).

Settings Menu Framework

In getting ready to add all types of settings (audio sliders, graphics and gameplay options, more multiplayer options), the menu system has been redesigned into a multi-panel system.

Because of the 3D nature of room-scale, the menu is unique (at least I haven't seen any other games do it yet) in that as you open up panels, the menu begins to wrap around you.

It keeps everything open as you traverse down into deeper options, allowing you to close and re-open the menu without requiring you to repeat the navigation steps.

It is not filled out yet (no additional features aside from the menu framework), but you will be able to see what is possible!

This week I'll be filling it out, so you won't have to wait too long for audio sliders and hand-offset toggles.

New Talent Tier

I want to begin experimenting with other systems for awarding talents (first thing will be a point buy where you use your score). To effectively do this I needed another tier of talents to get the full effect of awarding different levels of perk power.

So, the new talents in Tier 2 are:


     Chain Lightning: Enemies hit have a chance to arc electricity to 2 nearby enemies.
     Flint and Steel: Arrows drawn from the quiver have a chance to ignite themselves.
     Feather Fall: Arrows drop 50% slower.


These talents should all be fairly unique to each other and even the existing talents. I've done this to allow as much freedom as possible in trying different 'perk awarding' systems (even allowing you to pick perks from any tier). 

Hopefully none are too overpowered (I'm keeping an eye on feather fall to make sure it doesn't make people worse at the actual game).

Let me know if anything in the new menu breaks existing functionality, or if any of the new talents aren't working as intended.

notes.title: Alpha 0.7.0
notes.content:
Normally I would wait until Monday to roll out the week's big patch, but I need some bug testing done and I can fix things much faster over the weekend!

New Enemy System

This update brings with it a completely new enemy wave system. Previously each wave had the following attributes.


    Common Enemy
    2nd Common Enemy
    Single Spawn Enemies (list)
    isBoss (true/false)


That's it... I was able to get some pretty good use out of the Single Spawn enemies, by doubling up and such, but really it was an extremely simple system that didn't let me do anything interesting.

The new enemy system has a number of cool new features

[olist]
    Enemy spawn density curve (more enemies as waves increase)
    Enemy elite chance curve (more elites as waves increase)
    Flying Enemy spawn points
    List of potential enemy targets (currently unused, but future proofing)
[/olist]

And each wave has a much more generic approach, with a list of Enemy Chances. Each Enemy Chance has the following options


    Enemy Type
    Weight
    Single


The enemy type is fairly self explanatory, but the Weight and Single fields are the important part.

Single - Lets me guarantee a single instance of this enemy will occur somewhere during the wave.

Weight - A relative weight value for the chance to spawn the enemy type. (Ex, if I have two enemy types, both with a weight of 2, they each have a 50% chance to spawn. If I have 2 enemy types, one with a weight of 3 and one with a weight of 1, then the first has a 66% chance to spawn). Weights of SingleSpawn enemy types are ignored.

It's still pretty RNG based, but there should be much more interesting variation possible now.

This new system should also let anyone leave the game and continue uninterrupted. However, I can only test so much, which is why I am releasing this now. Would really like feedback on bugs/issues so I can fix them asap. There are definitely going to be some...

Other additions/fixes


    New flying enemy type
    Arrow stuck in bow should be fixed
    Talent nodes disappearing should be fixed
    Gate health should always correctly face player
    Boss attack distance increased (should stop from intersecting door)
    Boss health lowered slightly
    Tutorial progress reset for testing purposes (need it tested as well)

notes.title: QuiVr Alpha 0.6.0
notes.content:
Three big changes in today's update (and expect another update tonight fixing all the resulting broken things).

New Bosses

http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/25423482/4e3a6fc1e20dbf0a71a580a175731053d5dc11af.png

People were reaching much higher waves than I was anticipating, and after wave 20 it was a bit stale. I've increased some of the enemies difficulty, especially when scaling to 4 players, but the main change as been to add new bosses for waves 30, 40, and 50.

VRTK 2.0

QuiVr relies heavily on the SteamVR Toolkit. Previously, we were using version 0.8(ish, there weren't even version numbers back then...) and there were a lot of improvements being made that I was implementing myself, just in non optimal ways.

With the upgrade to VRTK 2.0 we should see more predictable behavior from controller interactions (Talent nodes selecting, arrow/quiver grabbint, etc).

Spectator Mode

The final big addition this week is the new Spectator Mode. It allows players to drop out of the combat, but not out of the game in the event that your arms are about to fall off ;). It can be accessed from the menu screen.

You are only allowed to become a spectator before a game has started (or after one has ended) and during the 15 second breaks between later waves. However, if you are already a spectator you can rejoin the fight at any time, even in the middle of a wave.

There are a number of smaller changes like brazier placement on the main platform and one or two performance improvements, but with the VRTK upgrade lots changed and needs to be tested again :)

Happy shooting!

notes.title: Alpha 0.5.6
notes.content:
Another fairly substantial update in the same day? Of course!

After playing with some people online and reading some more comments I got some great feedback on a number of topics and was able to implement a few of the suggestions pretty quickly.

The quiver change was substantial enough that I didn't want to wait until tomorrow to publish it ;)

So... here's some of the things that changed

Scores

The score system is now a bit more fleshed out. Each player will now be ranked according to an actual score formula. I won't spell out all the formulas that go into it, but here are the things that are taken into consideration.


    Shot distance (gradient)
    Shot distance (tiers ie. > 50m, > 100m)
    Headshots
    Talent procs
    Fire arrows


Would love to include style points (for things like getting a kill with a deflected arrow) but I'm not sure how I want to implement it yet. I will keep you posted!

Quiver Hitbox

A few people kept mentioning that it was hard to grab an arrow from the quiver, and asked if I could increase the hitbox... well the hitbox was already HUGE but I decided to add haptic feedback to let you know when your hand was inside the trigger volume.

Using that haptic feedback I was able to find a serious bug with the quiver, which was:

If you pulled back and released an arrow, if when you released, your hand was inside the Quiver trigger area, to grab an arrow you needed to move your hand out of the trigger area first, and then back in.

That is awful! And the only reason I didn't find it sooner is it totally depends on how you shoot if it affects you (and even then that's a pretty hard thing to put 2+2 together).

So, that's now been fixed and I scrapped the haptics because now I just can't imagine you won't be grabbing arrows all the time.

Arrow Draw

I went into The Lab's Longbow and did a bit more testing, and found that they were doing something really cool with the haptic feedback that I wasn't. The strength of the feedback depends on how far you draw the arrow back.

This has now been implemented, along with a new pull sound that better matches the timing of the haptic feedback which also gets louder the more you pull back.

Something that The Lab doesn't do, but I though would be a nice improvement is to also increase the pitch of the sound as the arrow is pulled back to imitate the increased tension on the string.

Teleportation Offset

One of the most requested features is allowing you to teleport manually. The reason for most people is disliking my 'stock' teleport positon, which puts ~half your playspace out in the middle of the air.

The reason for this is to have the center of your playspace where you should be standing (so that the game works regardless of room size). However, this results in a lot of wasted space if you have a big play area.

To fix this, I've created an offset system that looks at your room size and puts ~15% out over the edge of whatever platform you teleport to. This allows you to have enough room to peek over the edge comfortably without smashing into your wall, but at the same time allows you to explore a lot more of the teleport locations.

Smaller Changes/Additions


    Improved quiver performance (relating to issue above)
    Added subtle haptics when an enemy gets hit
    Added a 'core' to the arrows so they don't look hollow
    Multiplayer Keep healthbar should now sync correctly
    Enemy attack animations should play for non-hosts


Let me know if I broke anything! I can't really test multiplayer extensively anymore before pushing out updates as the system is too complex for a single computer to handle (voice chat often crashes the app if both try to access mic, and only one headset to do any actual VR testing)

notes.title: QuiVr Alpha 0.5.5
notes.content:
This update brings a new-user friendly experience as well as a full interface rework for the perk system :D

Tutorial
The first time you boot up the game will put you into the tutorial. It's fully voice over-ed (no subtitles yet but planned). And it will describe the basic mechanics of using the bow/quiver, teleporting, and the perk system. 

While the tutorial is playing you will not have access to the in-game menu (lots of things that could break the system, so better to just disable it for now)

After successfully completing it, it will no longer start you in it (saved state on local machine) when booting the game, but you can still access it from the in-game menu.

Perk System
While the tutorial explains how to use the system, I figure I can do it here as well.

Similar to the main menu, when you hit the touchpad on an empty controller the perk menu will come up in front of where you are looking. From there you can use the same empty hand to get more info and select perks.

The first perk will also become available at wave 5, and they all reset when a new game starts.

The system tracks the closest hand and zooms in on the tier that your hand is closest to.

Additionally, you can change the perk you've chosen at any time.

I think this system is much more intuitive than the previous one and would love feedback on it!

Other Changes

A couple other changes have also been made.


    Increased perk system performance when not visible
    Lowered number but increased difficulty of enemies (perf boost?)
    Fixed issue with rapid firing exploding arrows


Changes in last update (no patch notes -> debugging post)


    Fixed issue where beetle was not destroyed on death
    Increased size of stingray (increasing hitbox as well)
    Boss HP increased in multiplayer
    Score list resets on new game
    Score list correctly given in descending order

notes.title: The Case of the Missing Frames
notes.content:
Ok, so I've spent the past week working on performance improvements. It's not simple to debug a fairly complex scene, especially for VR where there's little prior knowledge to draw from and the requirements for "playable" are much more strict.

However, I think I've made a ton of progress and would like to share what I've done, and how I've gone about doing it so that other developers might not have to go through the same 'trial and error' as I have!

First, a general overview of what's required for VR: constant 90fps

That's all I'm going for, but that constant is important. 89 fps, even for an instant, just won't fly, which is why we should be aiming for 95 or so.

At 100fps we have 10ms per frame to work with, so that's been my target for rendering. We'll be talking in milliseconds (ms) from now on.

I'm using Unity3D to develop QuiVr, and it comes with a (not spectacularly intuitive) profiler to see how much time things cost per frame. This is primarily what I've been using to gauge performance hits/improvements. 

Base Line
Before we dig into the game's GPU/CPU times, we need to establish a baseline. Everything has overhead, including the profiler itself, so the first thing I needed to do was to see what the Unity Editor was taking up.

http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/25423482/cc8e955bb2a174c39870b6dd3d3e8061b34033c4.png

Here we can see that the editor (while not playing the game) has about a 5ms per frame hit with occasional spikes that immediately put our frame time out of the 10ms budget. That's fine (reprojection can handle it), but we just need to realize that spikes in the profiler while running the game may not actually be from the game itself.

Now it's time to profile the game when nothing is happening. Most people have reported that issues only occur when there are a fair few enemies in the game (Multiplayer has way more enemies on screen at a time), so I think we can assume that while not perfectly optimized, the base scene is ok.

Let's take a look at the CPU time:

http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/25423482/6bea77c7257445e47183a19511d08e1b01edefe4.png

That's pretty good. Our CPU is waiting for the GPU for a third of the time, so and even then we're around 200-150 fps in the editor (which has much higher overhead then a built executable)

Now lets look at the GPU (which were currently bound by)

http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/25423482/35b91430d97efe91f131bc0a1016465b4743ccde.png

That's not very helpful... About 2ms is being taken by rendering the static and skinned geometry, 0.2ms for setting render textures.... The other 7.8ms? ... Other

I can only speculate that I think the polling of the GPU and rendering this graph is taking a lot of the time, as I can hit the game much harder with graphics when the profiler is not running.

Can't get much more out of it than that, but we at least have a working baseline. 2.5ms of camera rendering on the CPU and 2ms of rendering on the GPU.

Let's get to some debugging!

Physics
Someone mentioned that they thought spiders were a potential cause for the issues, so I did what was reasonable and spawned in 20 spiders on top of each other. This was lucky

http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/25423482/a7b2746b61ca8021d257480b4ca1609d5821fef1.png

The profiler is showing 38ms on Physics processing...

After taking a look, it seems that my testing environment for ragdolls had leaked into the actual game, and the ragdoll physics were being calculated all the time! That is a simple enough fix, just turn the rigidbodies to kinematic (Animation overrides it which is why it doesn't act differently).

The results?
http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/25423482/a8119e82d4b7355000efb92ee40b82773925ced5.png

Over 5x performance improvement... but it's still 7ms which is way too much of our 10ms budget. Spreading the spiders out so they're not overlapping?

http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/25423482/1aaf417267d2f477a1bc20bf9380c5799b854df8.png

0.98ms is something I can live with for now, still 10% of our budget but the spiders have the most physics objects of any of the enemies by a huge margin (30 for the spiders as opposed to 7 for a ghoul).

However, that Animation.Update is 1.2ms, I don't like that at all...

Animation
Don't have any pictures for this one, but it turns out that every enemy had about 30 animations ready to play, when at most they need 7 (a couple attacks, idle, run, death).

Removing the extra animations from every enemy dropped that time down to ~0.2ms with 20 enemies in front of the low base.

The next thing I needed to check was that someone said that the Orcs were causing a serious issue.

Orcs
And boy were they right...

http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/25423482/98efc4d9a246404d1b939acb1a032facfbb56cce.png

8ms of animations for just 10 orcs on screen...

From the start, this looks like another animation problem, but if we open it up, it looks like there's some PhysX issue going on?

It turns out that I was using a mesh collider on the armor to make the arrows bounce off. And because the mesh was animated there was some serious calculations that needed to be made (even though the armor was only about 100 triangles). 

Turning that collider off dropped the physics down to 0.01ms and let me do this without dropping a single frame...

http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/25423482/506b934c46d46c6e5dc72d5ddd7e23fa6ff5582d.png

A bit hard to tell but the mini profiler is reporting 109fps with 40 animated orcs on screen.

Menu

Another thing I was able to find when digging through the baseline profiler was this...

http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/25423482/87d49953823b3e883e928afb8f3e8c08d199512f.png

over 5% of our budget is going to the EventSystem that drives the UI for the menu, that's silly if the menu isn't up, so that was able to be dropped to 0ms by disabling the EventSystem unless the menu is on screen.

Health Bars

Also in the UI department, health bars turn to face the player camera, which is actually a bit expensive to do every frame. Since the health bars aren't shown each frame, I set it to only rotate when visible, which was able to drop the Behavior.Update down to 0.5ms from 1.1ms.

Conclusion
There's still a fair bit to go, but these I think were some of the low hanging fruit that just needed a bit of digging to uncover and fix (and hopefully others can use this information as well!) so I wanted to show what I was doing to fix the issues.

Also in this patch
I've also done things like correctly list the scores in descending order, reset scores when a new game starts, and made the bosses faster and have more health.

The beetle has been fixed so that it should correctly despawn, the stingray has been made a bit larger, and a couple other detail changes have been made.

Please let me know if things are working better, and the more specific you can be about what causes the issue (spiders and orcs here were incredibly helpful) the better!

notes.title: Alpha 0.5.4
notes.content:
Huge CPU performance boost in multiplayer and a much requested feature!

Performance Boost
Apparently the UI text for the number of players (Players: 3/4) and connection status (joined) were taking up 3ms of the CPU time (11ms budget for 90fps), over 1/4 of the entire frame budget! Multiplayer Score Board
A multiplayer scoreboard has been added that tracks hits and headshots, so you can now track your progress against the other players in your game. It should be sorted high -> low, but I'm unable to test the MP on my own computer today so just let me know if it's opposite and I'll invert it!

As always, thanks for the continued feedback!

notes.title: Alpha 0.5.0
notes.content:
Thanks everyone for the continued feedback! Though I haven't been posting updates every day, I definitely have been working on the game. So without further ado I'd like to introduce Frostfall Keep.

Frostfall Keep
http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/25423482/adba21e192843ec018e334bf7dddc19e4365a760.png

It is both a Singleplayer and Multiplayer map with 5 unique vantage points and 5 different enemy routes. Each route is visible by differing degrees from the different vantage points.

The snowy aesthetic is both an artistic and design choice, as it looks fantastic in VR (solves some anti-aliasing problems) as well as provides sharp contrast from the approaching enemies, blood splatters, and magical effects.

There's too much to describe with just words, so jump in and check it out!

The other major feature included in this build is v0.1 of the talent system.

Talent System
Pressing the touchpad on your right hand will open up the talent system interface. Only the first set of talents are available, and are reset when changing between singleplayer and multiplayer.

The options can be chosen using the left hand, check them out to see what they do!

Thanks for the continued support and feedback. A lot of these changes haven't been tested in multiplayer (though they should work) so please let me know if there are any issues!

notes.title: QuiVr Alpha 0.4.3
notes.content:
This update adds a few tweaks and fixes as well as a rework of the fire system.

Changes and Fixes

    Voice chat disabled by default
    Voice chat threshold now higher to stop mic always on
    Hand fades when close to HMD


Fire System 1.0

The fire damage from arrows on fire has been completely reworked. Before it was a static damage boost to hit an enemy with a fire arrow. Now the effect is a damage over time. Enemies hit with fire arrows will "catch fire" for a length of time dependent on the enemy and take a variable amount of damage every 0.5 seconds during that time, hitting an enemy that is already on fire will refresh the DoT and immediately apply one tick of damage.

The system is now completely modular, with a "Flammable" component that allows anything (not just enemies) to be caught on fire if desired. It should also work in Multiplayer, though it has not been extensively tested.

notes.title: QuiVr Alpha 0.4.0
notes.content:
Thanks everyone for the continued testing, this week I'm extremely excited to bring you the first iteration of Multiplayer COOP!

 Multiplayer v0.1http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/25423482/4934ea8327aa04412dcdb0f234fa8d323cf53392.png
First and foremost, please keep in mind this is an initial version of multiplayer, so expect some bugs! (It's really hard to test multiplayer with only one Vive...)

To play, load up the game to the main scene, in the menu there is a new button that says "Multiplayer (testing)". Pressing it will take you to a new map and automatically connect you to a multiplayer game (if there isn't one available, it will create a new one). I've set it up this way to get you into the action ASAP, as I am assuming there will be few players on at any given time.

Currently there is no voice chat (though it is coming) and the map is very limited, no teleporters or anything, just a wall to defend. You should be able to pick up arrows people give you and play around with the physics barrel on the wall.

The room host (first person in) can start a new siege from the menu for the group to fight, it works identically to the singleplayer.

Enemy difficulty scales dynamically with the number of players, so the game is perfectly playable with 1, 2, 3, or 4 players (4 max per room).

Current known bugs:

    Losing a game will occasionally spawn the next wave anyway.


Please provide feedback on the multiplayer system so that I can improve it :)

Other Changes/Fixes


    Added initial loading scene while game fully loads
    Increased haptic feedback from grabbing and shooting arrows
    Fixed issue where enemies would not do damage on first hit
    Improved hand offset on drawing arrow
    Fixed left handed offset while drawing
    Improved particle system performance


Support email: support@alvios.com 
Leave feedback in discussions or the  Reddit thread

notes.title: Alpha 0.1.2
notes.content:
Sorry to hear about the continued crashes, I've just uploaded a new version that removes two things I saw in a number of crash-logs and reports:

1. Removed curved UI 
- This was a 3rd party system that I thought was cool, but it may have caused the issue, as many people reported crashing when bringing up the menu. And then on startup (after the instructions menu was added to startup).

2. Disabled graphics jobs
- Most people's crash-logs stopped at the enlighten thread startups. Graphics jobs are an experimental unity feature that makes rendering logic multithreaded. I am assuming that this experimental feature is the cause of the hard crashes on startup.

Small changes:
 - Moved quiver closer to player on startup
 - Increased quiver trigger radius by another 15%

Thanks for the feedback and patience as I work through these frustrating issues!
